etymology: Participle of affray: Old French esfreer, to frighten. Webster 1828: impressed with fear or apprehension; fearful; a lesser degree than terrified or frightened; followed by of before the object. The KJV uses it for guilt in the garden, for the saint who trusts while he is still afraid, and for the Lord’s command, be not afraid, when His presence is the reason.
biblical_def: Afraid in Scripture is not a mood to be managed. It is the creature answering a presence. Adam’s first word after the fall is this: I heard thy voice in the garden, and I was afraid, because I was naked; and I hid myself (Gen 3:10). That fear is guilt before the Holy, not a chemical event. David does not pretend the feeling is gone; he relocates it: What time I am afraid, I will trust in thee (Ps 56:3). Isaiah names the ground that ends it: Behold, God is my salvation; I will trust, and not be afraid (Isa 12:2). The LORD is light and strength, of whom shall I be afraid? (Ps 27:1). In the boat the object is a Person: Be of good cheer; it is I; be not afraid (Matt 14:27). The dictionary therefore keeps two fears from collapsing. The fear of the LORD is worship. Being afraid of nakedness, of men, of the night, of death, is the heart still measuring the wrong presence. The gospel does not scold the pulse into silence. It puts Jehovah in the place of the threat, and then says be not afraid because it is I.
webster_summary: Webster 1828 defines AFRAID as impressed with fear or apprehension; fearful. It expresses a less degree of fear than terrified or frightened, and is followed by of before the object of fear.
webster_full: AFRAID, a. [The participle of affray.] — Impressed with fear or apprehension; fearful. This word expresses a less degree of fear than terrified or frightened. It is followed by of before the object of fear; as, to be afraid of death.
Webster’s own illustration is moral, not theatrical: Joseph was afraid to sin against God.
scriptures: Genesis 3:10
And he said, I heard thy voice in the garden, and I was afraid, because I was naked; and I hid myself.
Psalm 56:3
What time I am afraid, I will trust in thee.
Isaiah 12:2
Behold, God is my salvation; I will trust, and not be afraid: for the LORD JEHOVAH is my strength and my song; he also is become my salvation.
Psalm 27:1
A Psalm of David. The LORD is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear? the LORD is the strength of my life; of whom shall I be afraid?
Matthew 14:27
But straightway Jesus spake unto them, saying, Be of good cheer; it is I; be not afraid.
corruption_summary: Afraid is corrupted when guilt before God is recast as a wellness problem, when stoic self-help pretends the saint need never feel it, and when “be not afraid” is sold as a vibe with the Speaker left out.
corruption_paragraphs: The first corruption is to medicalize Adam. Genesis 3:10 is nakedness and hiding, not a diagnosis. Wellness culture treats every fear as a symptom to soothe, and so it cannot hear the Lord’s voice in the garden. The recovery is confession: the first fear after the fall is guilt, and hiding is not healing.

The second corruption is Stoic and athletic courage that scolds the saint for still being afraid. Psalm 56:3 will not play that game. David is afraid, and in that hour he trusts. Christian manhood is not the absence of the pulse. It is trust while the pulse is still running. The fear of the LORD remains; being afraid of men is what faith dethrones.

The third corruption is to empty Matthew 14:27. Progressive unbelief and inspirational religion both like the slogan and drop the clause that carries it: it is I. Courage without Christ is still the boat in the dark. The Lord does not send a technique across the water. He sends Himself, and then He forbids fear.
roots_summary: English participle of affray (Old French esfreer). Verse-cache Strong’s on the quotations below: Hebrew yārē’ (H3372) at Ps 56:3; Hebrew pāḥad (H6342) at Isa 12:2 and Ps 27:1; Greek phobeō (G5399) at Matt 14:27. Genesis 3:10 is untagged in this cache; no Hebrew number is invented for it. The companion entry fear already treats the fear of the LORD as worship; this page is the English adjective afraid.
roots_lines: Hebrew yārē’ (H3372) — to fear, to revere (Ps 56:3, What time I am afraid).
Hebrew pāḥad (H6342) — to tremble, to be in dread (Isa 12:2; Ps 27:1, of whom shall I be afraid).
Greek phobeō (G5399) — to fear, to be afraid (Matt 14:27, be not afraid).
Genesis 3:10 untagged in this cache — no Hebrew number is minted for Adam’s I was afraid.
usage: Adam was afraid because he was naked — the first fear after the fall is guilt, not weather.
David is still afraid when he trusts (Ps 56:3); faith does not wait for the pulse to stop.
Be not afraid stands on it is I (Matt 14:27), not on a technique.

etymology: Old English nān: not one (ne + ān). Webster 1828: not one, of persons or things; not any; not a part; used as a substitute when the noun is omitted; formerly used before nouns where modern English says no. The KJV’s theological force is the empty set: none righteous, none else, none other name.
biblical_def: None in Scripture is a closed count. It does not mean “few,” and it does not mean “none except the decent.” Paul cites the Psalter as the anthropology of the race: There is none righteous, no, not one (Rom 3:10). That is total depravity in a pronoun. The same word fences the Godhead: I am God, and there is none else; I am God, and there is none like me (Isa 46:9); a just God and a Saviour; there is none beside me (Isa 45:21). The apostles carry it into the only Name: there is none other name under heaven given among men, whereby we must be saved (Acts 4:12). Our Lord will not even let “good” be shared: there is none good but one, that is, God (Mark 10:18). The dictionary therefore reads none as Scripture’s way of emptying the field so that grace, deity, and the Name stand alone. Where the age wants a crowded shelf — many righteous, many gods, many names, many goods — the Bible answers with a pronoun that will not share.
webster_summary: Webster 1828 defines NONE as not one, used of persons or things; not any; not a part; not the least portion. It is used as a substitute when the noun is omitted, and it may carry a plural sense.
webster_full: NONE, a. — Not one; used of persons or things. There is none that doeth good; no, not one. (Ps 14:1).
NONE, a. — Not any; not a part; not the least portion. It is used as a substitute, the noun being omitted. As a substitute, none has a plural signification.
Webster notes the older attributive use before nouns (now ordinarily no), and the idiom would none of me: utter refusal of counsel.
scriptures: Romans 3:10
As it is written, There is none righteous, no, not one:
Isaiah 46:9
Remember the former things of old: for I am God, and there is none else; I am God, and there is none like me,
Isaiah 45:21

Tell ye, and bring them near; yea, let them take counsel together: who hath declared this from ancient time? who hath told it from that time? have not I the LORD? and there is no God else beside me; a just God and a Saviour; there is none beside me.
Acts 4:12
Neither is there salvation in any other: for there is none other name under heaven given among men, whereby we must be saved.
Mark 10:18
And Jesus said unto him, Why callest thou me good? there is none good but one, that is, God.
corruption_summary: None is corrupted when universalism and moral self-report refill the empty set, when other names are set beside Jesus, and when “none else” is softened into a God among gods.
corruption_paragraphs: The first corruption is to put someone in the set Paul emptied. Universalism, annihilation-as-kindness, and the ordinary American creed (“I’m basically a good person”) all refuse Romans 3:10. None righteous means the race, in Adam, has no exception the sinner can nominate. The recovery is the doctrine of total depravity: the whole man fallen, and justification by an alien righteousness, not by finding a righteous remnant inside the self.

The second corruption is plural salvation. Interfaith hospitality, anonymous-Christian theories, and every scheme that treats Jesus as one saving name among others contradict Acts 4:12. None other name is not incivility. It is the exclusive claim of the risen Lord. The recovery is to preach that Name as the only one given, not as a brand among spiritual options.

The third corruption is to crowd the throne. Process theology and Open Theism make God a being among beings, learning, changing, competing. Isaiah 46:9 will not have it: none else, none like Him. Mark 10:18 will not share “good.” The recovery is classical theism: aseity, simplicity, the LORD who is, beside whom there is none.
roots_summary: Old English nān, not one. No number is invented for untagged English none elsewhere.
roots_lines: Greek ou (G3756) — no, not (Rom 3:10, There is none righteous).
Greek oute (G3777) — and not, neither (Acts 4:12, none other name — the cache tags the negative on none).
Greek oudeis (G3762) — no one, none (Mark 10:18, there is none good but one).
Hebrew ’ephes (H657) — end, nothing, none (Isa 46:9, there is none else).
Hebrew ’ayin (H369) — nothing, nought, there is not (Isa 45:21, there is none beside me).
usage: None righteous is the race in Adam — not a rude estimate, a closed count (Rom 3:10).
There is none else and none like Him (Isa 46:9); the throne is not a committee.
Salvation has none other name (Acts 4:12); goodness has none but God (Mark 10:18).

etymology: Old English withinnan: in the inner part. Webster 1828: in the inner part; in the limits or compass of; inwardly, internally; in the mind. The KJV uses it for the heart God renews, the law written inside, the fountain of evil that proceeds from the heart, and the kingdom the Pharisees wanted to pin on a map.
biblical_def: Within in Scripture names the inside that God sees and the inside that man cannot cleanse. David asks for a new creation there: Create in me a clean heart, O God; and renew a right spirit within me (Ps 51:10). The law is not only tablets: I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart (Ps 40:8). Our Lord will not let the Pharisees treat the kingdom as a GPS pin: the kingdom of God is within you (Luke 17:21) — not a spectacle they can point to, and not a permission to baptize unbelief as an inner light. The same adverb exposes religion that is only paint: sepulchres within full of dead men’s bones (Matt 23:27), and from within, out of the heart of men, the catalog of sins (Mark 7:21). The dictionary therefore refuses two swaps. Within is not the authentic self waiting to be expressed. It is the place that must be created anew, or it is the place that stays a grave. Indwelling is the Spirit’s work in the regenerate. It is not a kingdom already humming in every chest.
webster_summary: Webster 1828 defines WITHIN as a preposition: in the inner part; in the limits or compass of; not beyond. As an adverb: in the inner part; inwardly; internally; in the mind.
webster_full: WITHIN, prep. — In the inner part; as the space within the walls of a house; a man contented and happy within himself. In the limits or compass of; not beyond; used of place and time.
WITHIN, adv. — In the inner part; inwardly; internally. The wound festers within. In the mind.
scriptures: Psalm 51:10
Create in me a clean heart, O God; and renew a right spirit within me.
Psalm 40:8
I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart.
Luke 17:21
Neither shall they say, Lo here! or, lo there! for, behold, the kingdom of God is within you.
Mark 7:21
For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, murders,
Matthew 23:27
Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye are like unto whited sepulchres, which indeed appear beautiful outward, but are within full of dead men's bones, and of all uncleanness.
corruption_summary: Within is corrupted when Luke 17:21 is conscripted as New Thought (“the kingdom is already in you”), when the heart is treated as an authentic self to express rather than a fountain of sin to be remade, and when churches paint the sepulchre and call the paint discipleship.
corruption_paragraphs: The first corruption is the interiorized kingdom. New Thought, liberal Protestantism, and a strain of evangelical sloganeering take Luke 17:21 as proof that every person already contains the reign of God. Jesus is answering Pharisees who wanted a visible pin. He denies their map. He does not baptize unregenerate inwardness as the kingdom. The King was in their midst, and they would not have Him. The recovery is to keep the KJV wording and still refuse the swap: the kingdom is Christ’s rule, not the self’s glow.

The second corruption is expressive individualism. The age says the real you is within, and holiness is getting that self outside. Mark 7:21 says the opposite: from within proceed evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, murders. The heart is not a sanctuary of authenticity. It is a spring that must be made new (Ps 51:10) or it stays a grave. The recovery is regeneration, not self-expression.

The third corruption is the painted tomb. Platform religion, brand, and courtesy can be beautiful outward and still be within full of dead men’s bones (Matt 23:27). High-church aesthetic and low-church busywork both know how to whitewash. The recovery is the law within the heart (Ps 40:8) and a right spirit renewed, not a cleaner facade.

No number is invented for untagged English within elsewhere.

Greek entos (G1787) — within, inside (Luke 17:21, the kingdom of God is within you).
usage: Ask for a right spirit within (Ps 51:10) — the inside is created, not discovered.
The law within the heart is delight, not a private veto of the written Word (Ps 40:8).
From within proceeds the catalog of sins (Mark 7:21); paint on the tomb does not empty it (Matt 23:27).
